rationale:
Changed: Sunday is now fixed. Crete's cancelled and confirmed — 4 Oct is the club 4-mile (Shep calls it the Sharpness 4), so the two-scenario placeholder collapses to one. Three edits to that one entry: distance is now set at 6.437 km rather than left null, the pacing guidance is rewritten because he describes the course as lumpy — a flat 3:38-3:40/km target across an undulating four miles isn't right, same principle as the Cheltenham pacing note (course profile decides the shape, not forced even splits) — and the notes drop the Crete branch entirely. The team-prize angle he mentioned doesn't change the individual prescription: he was already racing this as a genuine effort, not a jog, so there's nothing to adjust there beyond noting it.

Everything else stands exactly as proposed on the 27th, because nothing else in his message touches it: the recovery week came through clean (achilles 0 every day, physio-flagged tightness resolved by Thursday, HRV/RHR back to normal, ACWR OPTIMAL/LOW throughout) — the trigger the last review named for resuming something sharper than pure easy running, short of the full Saturday/Wednesday spine because a hard session the day before a race is never right. Rebuild volume, one light neuromuscular touch Tuesday (6x200m at ~4-mile effort, full recovery between reps), strides Friday, easy shakeout Saturday. The four-week Guy Fawkes sharpening block still gets written next Sunday once this race is done, not guessed at today.

changes.notes: Rest - normal week rhythm resuming. Recovery week complete: achilles 0 every day, the physio-flagged tightness resolved, HRV and RHR back to normal range. Clean to build back up.
Easy 8km, conversational - continuing the rebuild toward norm volume.

First bit of speed since Cheltenham, deliberately light: 3km warm-up, 6x200m at ~4-mile effort (3:38-3:40/km) with FULL recovery between reps - jog/walk until actually recovered, not a fixed short rest, so every rep is fresh rather than accumulating fatigue - 3km cool-down. ~9-10km all in. This is a neuromuscular touch, not a return to the Saturday/Wednesday quality spine - that waits for the actual sharpening block once Sunday's race outcome is known.
Easy 6km. If a leg gym session is due this week, this is the point to have already had it - keep any heavy lower-body work at least 72h clear of Sunday, whichever race it turns out to be.
Easy 5km + 4-6 strides. Legs sharp for Sunday, not tired - strides stay controlled, not a speed session.
Easy 30-35 min shakeout, conversational throughout, no strides. The day before a race - whichever one it turns out to be - stays easy regardless.

CONFIRMED: club 4-mile road race (the Sharpness 4), Crete is off. A genuine shot at the club record (23:30-23:39) - projections sit at 23:17-23:20 blended, 23:02 off Cheltenham alone, so realistically inside 23:39 and a coin flip against 23:30 given two weeks removed from quality work. COURSE: he describes it as lumpy, so run it on effort, not a fixed pace - hold effort steady on the climbs rather than chasing 3:38-3:40/km through them, and let that pace come back on the descents rather than forcing an even split. The record itself was presumably set on this same course, so the benchmark doesn't need adjusting, only the pacing execution within the race. His habit of starting controlled and finishing quicker still suits this, lumps or not. There's a team prize on the line too, which he'd like to help with - that doesn't change anything here, he's already racing this flat out rather than treating it as a jog. Full protocol: Symbicort 20 min / salbutamol 15 min before gun, Puma Fast-R Nitro 3, proper 3km warm-up. Afterwards: 2-3 easy days into the Guy Fawkes block, no recovery week needed for a 4-mile.
